chunks: Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, who said:
A man asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, while I was with him, about an intoxicant and intoxicating nabīdh getting onto the garment. He said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: nabīdh; a fermented drink mentioned in legal discussions
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or problem

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rule about intoxicating nabīdh getting on one’s clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام regarding intoxicating liquid and nabīdh coming into contact with a garment. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no problem, making the narration relevant to discussions of ritual purity and impurity in fiqh.
